rows.question: How do I make up attendance hours?
rows.answer:
To make up attendance hours at Vista Ridge High School, you can:

- Attend AM or PM Study Halls (these count as double hours)
- Attend Saturday School (also counts as double hours)
- Participate in the Twilight program at the LEO campus (requires Counselor enrollment)

**Steps to document your make-up hours:**

1. Use the [Attendance Hours Tracking Form](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eI-X1hNFmoOk950AzDEihX01TWFFg-eL/view?usp=sharing) to record your hours. Forms are also available in the Assistant Principal (AP) office.
2. Have your supervisor or teacher print and sign their name on the form for each session.
3. Turn in the completed form to Joanna Norling or Micah Gillum in the Assistant Principal's office.

**Important notes:**
- Informal tutorials and community service are no longer accepted for making up hours.
- If you have special circumstances (like medical procedures), you can request an appeal by contacting your [Assistant Principal](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhs-assistant-principals-offi/home).

If you have any questions or need help with the process, reach out to your Assistant Principal.

rows.question: What is the student check-out policy?
rows.answer:
Here is the student check-out policy at Vista Ridge High School for the 2026-2027 school year:

- Parents/guardians must come to the main office in person, provide a valid photo ID, and sign their student out.
- Phone calls for early check-out are NOT accepted.
- All in-person early check-outs must occur before 2:45 pm. After 2:45 pm, early check-outs are not granted; students must wait for regular dismissal.
- Please arrive at least 20 minutes before you need your student to be released, due to high volume of requests.
- Students must sign in/out at the Attendance Window when leaving or returning to campus.
- On certain days (the Friday before Thanksgiving break, Winter break, Spring break, and the last day of school), early dismissal emails are not accepted. On these days, students must turn in a note to the Attendance Office before school begins to get their permit to leave.
- If you cannot provide notice before 10:30 a.m., you must come to the main office to sign your student out.

For more details, see the [How To Check Your Student Out Early](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhsattendance/student-sign-out) page. If you have further questions, you can contact the front office at 512-570-1800.
sources: 26-27 LISD Student & Parent Handbook (Student Handbook - English)

rows.question: How do I appeal an attendance decision?
rows.answer:
To appeal an attendance decision at Vista Ridge High School, here’s what you need to know based on the current school year’s information:

### Appealing Make-Up Hours (Hours Owed)
- If you owe hours due to falling below 90% attendance and believe there are extenuating circumstances (such as medical procedures or significant situations outside your control), you can request an appeal.
- Appeals can only be based on extenuating circumstances and must be supported by documentation (such as doctor’s notes or other relevant paperwork).
- To start the process, contact your Assistant Principal to discuss your situation and request an Attendance Appeal Request form. You can find their contact information on the [Assistant Principals page](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhs-assistant-principals-offi/home).
- Complete the appeal form and attach your supporting documentation.
- Submit the completed form to the Assistant Principal’s office.

### General Attendance Appeals (per district policy)
- A parent may write a letter of appeal to the campus Assistant Principal and turn it in to the registrar.
- Letters may be submitted at any time during the semester, but no later than ten (10) calendar days after the last day of classes for that semester.
- The Assistant Principal will review the appeal, considering attendance records, documentation, extenuating circumstances, and other relevant factors.
- If you disagree with the committee’s decision, you may appeal further to the school board by following policy FNG(LOCAL).

### Helpful Links
- [Attendance Appeal Request Form (Student Attendance Appeal Request 25_26)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uLdvXGyYp72w1Eu9_rMSpG1OaNUNbtSz/view?usp=sharing)
- [Hours Owed Information](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vistaridgehighschool/campus_information/hours-owed)
- [Attendance Office](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhsattendance/home)

If you have questions or need help with the process, contact your Assistant Principal or the Attendance Office. If you need to reach the front office for general guidance, their main number is 512-570-1800.

rows.question: How do I register for AP tests?
rows.answer:
To register for AP exams at Vista Ridge High School for the 2026-2027 school year, you must complete all three steps below by October 28, 2026, to avoid a late fee:

1. **Register and Pay**
   - Go to the [Total Registration Link](https://user.totalregistration.net/AP/441176) and complete your exam registration.
   - Pay the exam fee ($85 per exam, or $15 per exam for eligible Free/Reduced Lunch students).

2. **Join AP Classroom**
   - Join your specific AP Classroom section(s) on the College Board website using the unique join code provided by your teacher or in your Total Registration confirmation email.
   - [College Board's AP Classroom](https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/access-your-ap-resources/join-your-class-online)

3. **Confirm Your Exam in AP Classroom**
   - In AP Classroom, select "YES" to indicate you are taking the AP exam for each course.
   - [Instructions: Enroll in AP Class and Indicate Exam](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rJ644R4UCWc7EZcqZiYABLmxSvolSxPBijn8T-ZA3v4/edit?usp=sharing)

**Important:**  
- Both registration/payment in Total Registration and confirmation in AP Classroom are required for each exam.
- If you miss the October 28 deadline, a late fee will apply.

For more details and step-by-step instructions, visit the [Vista Ridge Advanced Placement Website](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/advanced-placement/home) or see the [AP Test Registration Info](https://vrhs.leanderisd.org/ap-test-registration).

rows.question: What do seniors need to do before graduation?
rows.answer:
Here are the main things Vista Ridge High School seniors need to do before graduation, based on the information for the Class of 2027:

- **Complete the FAFSA:** Filling out the FAFSA is a high school graduation requirement. The application opens October 1st, and the priority deadline for most Texas universities is January 15th. Check each university for their specific deadlines. [FAFSA](https://studentaid.gov/)

- **Order Cap and Gown:** Seniors must order their Cap, Gown & Tassel Unit (the only required item) through Herff Jones. Details and the order link will be provided by the school.

- **Clear All Obligations and Hours:** All obligations and hours must be cleared before picking up your cap and gown.

- **Attend Graduation Practice:** Seniors are expected to attend graduation practice and the "Clap Out" immediately following practice.

- **Follow Cap Decorating Guidelines:** If you plan to decorate your graduation cap, follow the [Cap Decorating Guidelines](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18flNuM9zS485RP3ismFk8OnI2CpZp0p9VaXOWS7RxFU/edit?tab=t.0).

- **Monitor Progress Toward Graduation:** Make sure you are on track to complete all graduation requirements as outlined in the Student Handbook and by your counselor.

- **Check for Senior Events:** Participate in senior events such as the panoramic picture, prom, Senior SAIL, and Senior Awards (invitation only).

- **Preorder Graduation Pictures:** Information will be provided on how to preorder your graduation pictures.

- **Review the Post High School Checklist:** Use the [Post High School Checklist](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gZ43iD9wiXcQPqEume779vCEFwQmGh8F_cf0BhLVSv8/edit?usp=sharing) to make sure you have completed all necessary steps for life after graduation.

For more details or if you have specific questions, you can refer to the [Seniors 2027](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vistaridgehighschool/seniors-2027) page or contact your counselor.

rows.question: What is Ranger Time?
rows.answer:
Ranger Time at Vista Ridge High School is a flexible period built into the school day, held from 9:45am to 10:15am on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. During Ranger Time, students can:

- Register for specific activities such as clubs, tutorials, or workshops
- Be assigned to mandatory meetings or academic support by teachers

This period is designed to give students opportunities for academic help, personal growth, and involvement in campus life. Registration for activities is done through the Flex-Time menu in the Ranger Time Portal, which you can access here: [Ranger Time Portal](https://adv.leanderisd.org/login.aspx?ReturnUrl=%2fDefault.aspx).

For more details, you can visit the [MINGA 101 - Ranger Time (Flex)](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhsminga-101/ranger-time-flex) page.

rows.question: How do I report bullying?
rows.answer:
You can report bullying at Vista Ridge High School in several ways:

- Notify a teacher, school counselor, principal, or any other district employee as soon as possible.
- You can also report bullying anonymously online at [Anonymous Alerts for Leander ISD](https://www.anonymousalerts.com/leanderisd/).

The administration will investigate any allegations of bullying and related misconduct. If you have questions or concerns, you are encouraged to discuss them with a teacher, counselor, principal, or the office of Student Support Services at 512-570-0150.

For more information, you can visit the district’s [Bullying Prevention](https://www.leanderisd.org/bullying) page.

rows.question: How do I access my STAAR scores?
rows.answer:
You can access your STAAR scores in two main ways:

### 1. Through the Texas Assessment Parent Portal
- Go to [TexasAssessment.gov](https://www.texasassessment.gov/staar.html).
- Click "Log In to Parent Portal."
- Enter your child’s Unique Access Code and date of birth.
    - If you don’t know the access code, click "How do I find my access code?" and enter your child’s legal first name, TSDS ID (or SSN), and date of birth.
- View your scores and download the Confidential Student Report (CSR).

### 2. Through the Home Access Center (HAC)
- Log into your [LISD Home Access Center (HAC)](https://www.leanderisd.org/homeaccess).
- Click on the Grades icon at the top.
- Next to Report Card on the left, click on Texas Test Scores.
- Your results will appear, or you’ll be directed to the Texas Student Portal.

### Need Help?
If you have trouble accessing your scores or have questions about your results, you can contact:
- Campus Testing Coordinator: Linsey Cernero | 512-570-1823 | linsey.cernero@leanderisd.org
- Principal: Keith Morgan | 512-570-1810 | keith.morgan@leanderisd.org

You can also find step-by-step instructions in English and Spanish here:
- [Parent Instructions: HAC (English)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gjw-eI37OPctz_CnqsSQbwPhIrcBWmGwaKzsj47wwyM/edit?tab=t.0)
- [Parent Instructions: TX Assessment Portal (English)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-FYpAMvoDN5DjGZD3ThvecRfWtAJCnss/view?usp=sharing)
